clue.text: Bad social network site abroad — and that's definite

parts.note: bad as in feeling poorly, unwell
Bebo was a social networking website popular in the 2000s
und is the German word for and, so 'and' said abroad

explanation.surface: Someone declares a foreign social media site bad, and insists they are sure of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to translate 'and' into a foreign language: German UND.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'I'll be bound' is an emphatic way of saying one is certain, so it means something is definite.

clue.text: Joke about African runner upset Phil's wife

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the river's name upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: a runner is a river; the Nile is Africa's great river
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, was the wife of Prince Philip

explanation.surface: A quip about an African athlete has offended Phil's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African runner' suggests an athlete, but it is a river: NILE, turned up by 'upset' to make ELIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, single-sentence gag is a classic kind of joke, a synonym in everyday comedy talk.

clue.text: Bank being extremely heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle letters, the heart of the word

parts.note: really means extremely, very

explanation.surface: A bank is accused of being utterly without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central AL of REALLY. 'Bank' is a verb here, as in banking on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on or trust them, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Certain characters somehow having time to socialise

indicators.note: somehow says the letters fall into some unspecified new order

explanation.surface: Some characters manage to find time for socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CERTAIN with T.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix and communicate with others is to socialise, a close synonym.

clue.text: Film host in boudoir? Maybe

indicators.note: in places the host inside the room

parts.note: a boudoir is a lady's private room; 'Maybe' marks it as just one example
MC, master of ceremonies, is a host

explanation.surface: A film where a host turns up in a bedroom, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' says a boudoir is only one kind of ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic comedy, shortened to its familiar two-syllable nickname, is a genre of movie.

clue.text: Modest musician scented shameful U-turn by insiders

indicators.note: insiders says the turned word goes inside the scented one

parts.note: musky means having a heavy scent

indicators.note: a U-turn turns the word back the other way

parts.note: gross means flagrant, shameful

explanation.surface: A shy musician, perfumed, is caught in a shameful policy reversal by people on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modest' is the composer's first name, not a description of him. 'U-turn' makes SSORG; 'insiders' puts it within the scented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest Mussorgsky was the Russian composer of Pictures at an Exhibition, so he is a musician named Modest.

clue.text: Benefit from learning about computers etc with academic

parts.note: a prof, professor, is an academic
IT, information technology, is the school subject about computers

explanation.surface: Someone gains from studying computing alongside a lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain or benefit from something is to profit by it, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Government-appointed 'expert' gets a right stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing signals the letters filling the middle of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A government adviser gets a real hammering from critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffing' sounds like a beating but marks the letters inside 'geTS A Right'.
explanation.definitionFit: British papers call a minister's appointed specialist adviser a drugs or energy czar, after the old Russian ruler.

clue.text: Light left on before service

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A lamp is left burning before a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like worship but is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp with a protective case, carried or hung, is a kind of light.

clue.text: Overuse unfamiliar works

indicators.note: unfamiliar says the word appears in a strange, rearranged form

explanation.surface: Using an unfamiliar word too much is a stylistic fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' rearranges OVERUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: French for works, the collected output of an artist or writer, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Blooming brave but pointless

indicators.note: pointless removes a compass point, here S for south

parts.note: ballsy is slang for bold, brave

explanation.surface: Someone flourishing and courageous, yet achieving nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops S (south, a point of the compass) from BALLSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bally is a mild British euphemistic intensifier, like 'blooming' or 'flipping'.

clue.text: Poor example of 10,4 using Word — see a bit of criticism flying round

indicators.note: flying round describes letters whirling about into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
the number written out as a word

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A poor attempt at writing numbers in a word processor draws criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying round' shuffles all four pieces together. 'using Word' hints that the 4 is spelt out as a word rather than a digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something 'an apology for' or 'a travesty of' a thing means it is a poor specimen of it.

clue.text: He may not get on with ladies' man on the surface, but partner's very forward

indicators.note: very forward places this piece right at the front

parts.note: Scots 'but and ben' is a two-room cottage, so ben is the partner of but

indicators.note: the ladies' man forms the outside, the surface, with the other letter inside

parts.note: a charmer is a man who woos women

explanation.surface: A man who doesn't get on with a womaniser, while his partner is very pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but partner' needs the Scots phrase 'but and ben' (outer and inner room of a cottage). W goes inside CHARMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who sits on the sidelines and is never sent on to play may not get on the pitch.

clue.text: Run off under the influence in Bristol — trouble

parts.note: high means intoxicated, under the influence

indicators.note: in puts the trouble inside the slang word

parts.note: rhyming slang: Bristol Cities for titties, so a Bristol is a tit
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone drunk in Bristol gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristol' is not the city but Cockney rhyming slang: Bristol City rhymes with titty. 'in' places the trouble inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hightail it is American slang for fleeing in a hurry, so it means to run off.

clue.text: Little amphibian's not old

indicators.note: not says the old letter is to be left out

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A small amphibian is a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not old' removes O from TOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, a bit, is a little: a noun synonym, as in 'a little more'.

clue.text: Political work with Democrat — question a mate about it

parts.note: to ask is to question

indicators.note: the mate goes about, around, the word it

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A politician works with a Democrat, asking a friend about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the mate surrounds the word 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx's critique of capitalism is the most famous work of political economy.

clue.text: Bombed insurgent's house — it's immoral

definitions.note: the phrase stands for a noun: the quality of being immoral

indicators.note: a bombed building is blasted apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: An insurgent's home has been bombed, an act called immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombed' rearranges INSURGENTSHOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness, sinfulness: the quality of being immoral or unjust.

clue.text: Big boss's girlfriend getting head down? No way!

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, of the girlfriend word goes down, to the bottom

parts.note: a lover is a girlfriend
O is nothing, zero, so no
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: The boss's girlfriend sleeps at work, prompting disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting head down' moves the first letter of LOVER to the end, making OVERL.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme ruler or master over others is a big boss.

clue.text: Marks on back of one dress suspicious

indicators.note: suspicious here means fishy, not as it should be, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Marks on the back of a frock look suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicious' rearranges ONEDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cheque or document is literally to sign on its reverse.

clue.text: Call friend over

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, back to front

parts.note: bud is an informal word for friend

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a friend to come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses BUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To name or nickname someone is to call them something, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Attachment to Football League team

definitions.meaning: an extra component fixed on afterwards
... Wanderers, an English football club from Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt-on is an add-on accessory; Bolton Wanderers are an English Football League club.

clue.text: Hated bonking each one when engaged? I don't think so!

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so these letters go into the scrambled word
bonking, hitting or bashing, knocks the letters into a new order

parts.note: every means each
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they hated having sex with every partner while engaged, then denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonking' rearranges the first word to THDEA; 'when engaged' tucks the next two pieces inside it, after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of indignant disbelief or refusal, rejecting a suggestion outright.

clue.text: Change to green at last — surely that means go

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters
at last picks out only the final letter

explanation.surface: A traffic light turning green surely means you can move off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges GREEN to ENERG; 'at last' takes Y from 'surely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or drive, as in 'full of go', a synonym.

clue.text: OK to hold current rise over? NO!

indicators.note: to hold means the first word contains what follows

parts.note: well means OK, fine
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: over turns the word back to front

parts.note: a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A query about whether it is fine for a current to keep rising, met with refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the rise into LLIH; 'to hold' puts current plus that inside the OK word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse emphatic British refusal, the opposite of agreeing to do something.

clue.text: Understanding reasons for report

indicators.note: for report signals a word as it would be heard when spoken

parts.note: whys are reasons, as in the whys and wherefores

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the reasons behind a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' is an adjective here, meaning shrewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sagacious and perceptive is wise, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Hurt when doing the same thing with nothing on — language!

indicators.note: on puts the nothing piece on, ahead of, the injury

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all

parts.words: Hurt when doing the same thing
parts.note: RSI, repetitive strain injury, is hurt caused by doing the same action repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone stubs a toe while naked and swears, prompting a shout of 'Language!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing, a euphemism for a rude phrase. 'language!' is the definition, not a rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of Iran is Persian, also known by this name.

clue.text: Most liked 'wild beast' except for you

indicators.note: except for says the letter for you is left out

parts.note: fauve is French for wild beast, the name given to Matisse and the Fauvist painters
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Everyone's favourite is the 'wild beast', apart from you.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint at a translation: French 'fauve'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form of favourite, the one preferred above others.

clue.text: Talk to police about who vandalised display

indicators.note: about says the informer word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells the police who vandalised a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges the clue's 'who' to HOW; 'about' wraps the informing word around it. 'Talk to police' means inform, slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition or screening is a showing of something, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Struggle to take in atmosphere round holiday hotspot

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the turned word
round says the word is turned around, back to front

parts.note: air is atmosphere
to vie is to struggle or compete
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: People fight for space and a bit of air at a crowded resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns atmosphere into RIA; 'in' puts struggle plus take inside it, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean coastline is a famous resort area for sunny breaks.
